title: Writers Writing, Readers Reading, Creators Creating

reader_summary.source_label: From the episode notes — transcript not yet available
reader_summary.headline: We've been financing good writing with bad advertising -- and "attention monsters" (to quote Craig Mod) for way too long.
reader_summary.overview: We've been financing good writing with bad advertising -- and "attention monsters" (to quote Craig Mod) for way too long. So what happens when the technology for creators finally falls into place? We're finally starting to see shift in power away from publications as the sole gatekeepers of talent, towards individual writers.

key_points.text: Especially when the best possible predictor of the value of a piece of writing is, well, the writer .
The publication's brand is no longer the guarantee of quality, or the only entity we should be paying and be loyal to.
how do they find signal in the noisy world of drive-by billboard advertising, "attention-monster" feeds, and the death of Google Reader?
